# National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH)

> NCCIH is the NIH's lead agency for scientific research on complementary and integrative health approaches, providing evidence-based information, clinical resources, and funding for studies on pain management, natural products, and whole-person health.

NCCIH (part of the National Institutes of Health) conducts and supports rigorous scientific research on complementary health practices including acupuncture, herbal medicine, yoga, and other integrative approaches. The center serves both consumers seeking reliable health information and researchers pursuing complementary medicine studies.

## Key Topics

- Complementary and integrative health
- Pain research and management
- Clinical trials
- Dietary supplements

- Whole Person Health

## Core Resources

- [Home](https://www.nccih.nih.gov): NCCIH homepage providing complementary and integrative health information and research resources.
- [Health Info Home](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health): Hub for complementary health information, consumer education, and clinical trial resources.
- [Research Home](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research): NCCIH research overview covering extramural and intramural research programs and funding.

## Consumer Health Information

- [Topics A-Z](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/atoz): A-Z directory of complementary health topics including acupuncture, herbs, and wellness practices.
- [What Is Complementary, Alternative, or Integrative Health?](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/complementary-alternative-or-integrative-health-whats-in-a-name): Definitions and introduction to complementary, alternative, and integrative health approaches.
- [Pain](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/pain): Pain management information and NCCIH research programs for consumers and health professionals.
- [Safety Information](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/safety): Safety guidance for complementary health products, drug interactions, and herbal medicines.
- [Know the Science](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/know-science): Tools for understanding health research and making evidence-based health decisions.
- [Tips on Complementary Health](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tips): Consumer tips and guidance for evaluating complementary health practices and dietary supplements.
- [Información en Español](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/espanol): Spanish-language health information on complementary and integrative medicine from NCCIH.

## Research Programs

- [Division of Extramural Research](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/extramural): Information on NCCIH extramural research grants, funding, and research sponsorship programs.
- [Division of Intramural Research](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/intramural): NCCIH intramural research division overview focusing on pain and nervous system research.
- [NIH Pain Research Center](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/nih-pain-research-center): NIH-wide multidisciplinary pain research center studying mechanisms and nonopioid treatments.

## Research Resources & Results

- [Research Results by Date](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/research-results): Plain language summaries of NCCIH-supported and conducted complementary health studies.
- [Clinical Trials](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/clinicaltrials): Information on NCCIH clinical trials, ClinicalTrials.gov, and volunteer recruitment.
- [Resources for Researchers](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/resources): Clinical research tools, Whole Person Health Index, and systematic review resources for researchers.
- [Statistics on Use](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/statistics-on-complementary-and-integrative-health-approaches): National survey data on Americans' use of complementary health approaches from NHIS and NHANES.

## Professional Resources

- [Resources for Health Care Professionals](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/providers): Evidence-based clinical resources and guidelines for healthcare providers on complementary health.

## News & Updates

- [NCCIH Research Blog](https://www.nccih.nih.gov/research/blog): Blog covering NCCIH research developments, funding opportunities, and complementary health research.
